attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, given in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: commitments of over $718B to the three hyperscalers, and that neither lab can afford them. 'Hyperscalers' is a fair stand-in for Microsoft, Amazon and Google.

contract.note: The contract reads affordability as the ability to pay when due, using available resources and financing. That is a fair, ordinary reading. The result turns on it and on treating announced face values as the commitment stock.

evidence.note: Reports the $250B OpenAI Azure commitment. One component only; says nothing on affordability.
Amazon disclosure: $38B plus $100B for OpenAI on AWS. Multiyear component.
Anthropic disclosure of the $30B Azure commitment. Component only.
Anthropic's April 2026 announcement includes more than $100B over ten years with AWS. Component only; no payment schedule.
Reuters relays a reported $200B Google commitment that Reuters could not verify. With the other components, the total exceeds $718B on face values.
Anthropic's $30B Series G raise is a financing resource that bears against inability to pay. It does not prove the obligations are affordable.

reviews.rationale: Announced and reported face values add up to more than $718B, but one component is unverified and nothing reconciles remaining balances. The affordability half is untested: there are no payment schedules or cash and financing comparisons, and e9 shows significant financing. The support condition needs both parts. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the $718B commitment, the claim that the labs cannot survive without VC funding, and the 'because' link to losing money on every transaction.

contract.note: Reading 'lose money on every transaction' as transactions failing to cover the cost of supplying them is ordinary and fair. Reading survival dependence as a financing counterfactual is also fair. The result turns on the cost definition, which the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Microsoft confirms the incremental $250B OpenAI Azure commitment. Component only.
Amazon: $38B plus $100B for OpenAI on AWS. Component only.
NVIDIA joint release: Anthropic's $30B Azure commitment.
Amazon's equity investment in Anthropic, plus its AWS commitment of more than $100B. Shows outside funding, not that the funding is indispensable.
Reported $200B Google commitment, unverified by Reuters. The reconstructed total is about $718B.

Secondary report: OpenAI's Q1 2026 gross margin was 39%, with large cash holdings. This weighs against losses on every transaction and against immediate funding dependence. The cost definition is unknown, the source documents are unavailable, and it covers OpenAI only.

reviews.rationale: The commitment total can be roughly rebuilt from announced and reported values, though one is unverified. The packet has no transaction-level cost records for either lab and no financing counterfactual. The secondary report of a positive OpenAI gross margin (e6) points against the claim but cannot settle transaction economics. The causal link is neither established nor disproved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Adding 'from it' (AI profit) matches the context, which is about the AI system making more money than it costs. 'Non-stop' is rhetorical emphasis.

contract.note: Reading 'can show a profit' as publicly demonstrating AI-specific profit is fair given the context. Consolidated profits would plainly defeat the claim, so the result turns on the AI-specific reading. The company set is uncertain.

evidence.note: AWS segment is profitable in Q1 2026, but AI revenue and costs are not isolated.
Google Cloud is profitable, but shared AI R&D costs sit outside the segment, so no AI-specific profit is shown.
Microsoft Intelligent Cloud has a 40% margin, covering non-AI activity too. No separately costed AI profit.

reviews.rationale: None of the three hyperscaler disclosures in the packet isolates AI profit. That is consistent with the claim for those firms. But Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic were not reviewed, so the support condition's 'sufficiently complete review' is not met, and no item shows a disclosed AI-specific profit. The outcome is open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He asserts that unnamed sources lied.

semantics.note: Keeps 'I think', the charge of lying and the mathematical reasoning. Here 'I think' with 'at this point' is a firm stated belief about past facts, not a probability hedge.

contract.note: Reading 'made' as realized 2025 revenue is fair and ordinary. The clause that treats a GAAP figure as context unless it is reconciled to the press-estimate basis is protective of the speaker, and the result turns on it.

evidence.note: A news report of the S-1 gives audited 2025 revenue of $4.6B. That weighs heavily against the claim that $4.5B made no mathematical sense. It is held as context because its GAAP basis is not reconciled to the estimate basis the contract requires.

reviews.rationale: The only item reports audited 2025 revenue of $4.6B, close to the challenged $4.5B, which strongly undercuts the speaker's arithmetic. The contract and the basis rule keep a GAAP figure as context until it is reconciled to the press estimate, and that has not been done. Nothing addresses whether the sources knowingly lied. The packet does not formally settle the claim.
